title: What If a City Went Seven Years With No Traffic Deaths?

scenes.text: What if a whole city had no traffic deaths for seven years? One crowded city did.
Hoboken, New Jersey, is home to nearly 60,000 people and ranks fourth for density in the country.
Since January 2017, no driver, cyclist or pedestrian has died in traffic there.
The secret was boring. The city banned parking near corners so drivers could see people crossing.
It added 418 markers for clear corners, and set 15 mile an hour school zones on 67 blocks.
No miracle tech. Just wider curbs, shorter crossings and slower cars, which is why other cities copy it.

description:

Hoboken, New Jersey, did it since January 2017 with clear corners, wider curbs and slower school zones.
